clue.text: Missing first dance, policeman comes in for a drink

indicators.note: the policeman enters the middle of what is left of the dance, so it surrounds him
missing its first means the opening letter of the dance is dropped

parts.note: a galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance
cop is slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A police officer skips the opening dance at a party and heads inside for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing first dance' reads as someone arriving late to a party; it actually tells you to behead a dance name. A galop is a fast ballroom dance of the 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet, fruit-flavoured alcoholic beverage sold ready-mixed in bottles, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Father in charge in car club on the continent

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the club's initials

parts.note: the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation
Fr is the abbreviation for a priest called Father
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A priest, put in charge of a motoring club, travels abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' appears twice: the one inside 'in charge' belongs to that abbreviation, the second is the instruction to put things inside. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is one of the seven continents, the second largest by area.

clue.text: Commons' leader leaving in wooden box

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Commons
someone who is off is leaving or departing
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Leader of the House of Commons departs, carried out in a wooden box.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffin is the wooden box in which a dead body is buried or cremated.

clue.text: Strains of carol Pete's arranged

indicators.note: arranged as in music, the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The melody of a Christmas carol that Pete has arranged for singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strains' and 'arranged' both point to music, but strains is a verb meaning filters.
explanation.definitionFit: Percolates means passes liquid through a filter, as coffee does, which is a sense of strains.

clue.text: Cooked tapas and ziti, say

indicators.note: cooked food is altered from its raw form, so the letters are changed round

parts.note: Spanish snacks, taken as written

explanation.surface: A menu of cooked Spanish snacks and a dish of ziti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks ziti as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ziti are long tubes of Italian pasta, so ziti is an example of the category.

clue.text: Empty three-master of the late Renaissance?

indicators.note: empty stands for nothing, a ring-shaped zero, placed within the ship's name

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship with three masts
nothing at all, shown as the round letter that looks like zero

explanation.surface: An abandoned old sailing ship dating from the end of the Renaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like an adjective for the ship, but it supplies the O that goes inside BARQUE. The question mark admits the definition is loose: the Baroque period followed on from the late Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque is the ornate style in art and music that grew out of the late Renaissance around 1600, hence the hedging question mark.

clue.text: Perhaps Brownie pack arrived with artillery

parts.note: to box goods is to pack them
came means arrived
RA is the Royal Artillery of the British Army

explanation.surface: A Brownie pack turns up accompanied by heavy guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brownie pack' suggests a troop of junior Girl Guides; the Brownie is instead Kodak's famous cheap camera and 'pack' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodak Brownie was a simple, cheap box-shaped camera, so it is one example of the type.

clue.text: String of Pearls — part of Meyerbeer opera

indicators.note: part of means the letters lie inside a longer run of the clue's words

parts.note: spans the end of the composer's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A piece of music titled String of Pearls taken from an opera by Meyerbeer.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like a song title, but it is simply a string of pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: A long strand of pearls worn as a necklace is called a rope of pearls.

clue.text: Intelligence rating that results from division

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Q in IQ, a measured score of mental ability
second meaning: the answer you get when one number is divided by another

explanation.surface: An IQ score that comes from splitting things up.
explanation.definitionFit: IQ stands for intelligence quotient, and in arithmetic the quotient is the result of dividing one number by another.

clue.text: Looks closely at Cockney cocktails

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops initial h, so the word is heard as said in East London

parts.note: highballs are tall cocktails, said without the h

explanation.surface: Someone stares hard at the drinks in a London East End bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, the traditional working-class Londoners, famously drop the h, so highballs comes out sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to look at it hard and closely, an informal verb.

clue.text: Look it up, either way

indicators.note: either way says the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: to consult a reference book or source

explanation.surface: A friendly instruction to check something in a reference book, whichever way you go about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is only a comment on the answer: the five letters are the same read in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to a dictionary or manual is to consult it, which is what looking something up means.

clue.text: Old invader cut call for Charlie Parker's instrument

indicators.note: cut means the word is trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: the Saxons invaded Britain after the Romans left
to phone someone is to call them

explanation.surface: An ancient raider cut short a phone call meant for a famous jazz musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old invader' points to the early Germanic settlers of England rather than any Viking or Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Parker was the great bebop jazz player whose instrument was the alto saxophone.

clue.text: Bangers and mash from a hospital chef for starters

indicators.note: to mash is to crush and mix, so these letters are pulped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: for starters means only the first letter of the chef is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of chef

explanation.surface: Sausages and mashed potato served up by a hospital cook as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bangers and mash' reads as a single dish, but the phrase splits: 'Bangers' is the definition and 'mash' the anagram signal. Bangers are British slang for sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipolatas are small thin sausages, and banger is the everyday British word for a sausage.

clue.text: An Indian, oddly, appearing in opera

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a

indicators.note: oddly means only the letters in odd positions of the word are kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of Indian

explanation.surface: A man from India behaves strangely while appearing in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt, about an enslaved Ethiopian princess.

clue.text: Cold meal prison dished up

indicators.note: food dished up is served in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A chilly dinner served to inmates in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold meal' reads as one phrase about food; 'Cold' alone is the definition, in the sense of unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is distant and unfriendly, lacking personal warmth, which is what impersonal describes.

clue.text: Publicise new tramline for transport interchange

parts.note: to air an idea is to make it public

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A transport authority advertises a new tram route linking up with other services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New tramline' sits naturally in a transport story, which hides that 'new' tells you to rearrange the tramline's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An air terminal is the airport building where passengers switch between planes and ground transport, a kind of interchange.

clue.text: Cad died before noon in Dutch port

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a dishonourable man
d is the abbreviation for died
a.m. means before midday

explanation.surface: A scoundrel died one morning in a harbour city in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is the main seaport of the Netherlands and one of the busiest in Europe.

clue.text: Calm, having made up?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: having created, as with music or a poem

explanation.surface: Feeling at peace after patching up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' suggests reconciling or wearing make-up, but here it means invented or written.
explanation.definitionFit: A composed person is serene, and a composer is someone who has made up a piece of music.

clue.text: A boss of a detective department who's hooked?

parts.note: taken as written
the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force
the head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: Asks whether the chief of a police detective unit is addicted to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police. The boss comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidhead is slang for a habitual user of LSD, someone hooked on the drug.

clue.text: Arrange part of Sachertorte, crumbling

indicators.note: a cake that is crumbling falls apart, so its letters break up and regroup

parts.note: the Viennese chocolate cake, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a piece of Viennese chocolate cake that is falling to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' tempts you to look for a hidden word, but all eleven letters of Sachertorte are used; 'part of' only nods to music written in orchestral parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to score music for an orchestra, and more broadly to organise or coordinate something carefully.

clue.text: Island ways reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so it is what is heard that counts

parts.note: roads are ways to travel

explanation.surface: The routes around an island, as described in a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a large Greek island in the Aegean, near the Turkish coast.

clue.text: Genuine manuscript showing spheres of activity

parts.note: real means genuine
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: An authentic old manuscript revealing someone's areas of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are fields or domains of interest or action, the same idea as spheres.

clue.text: Coffee machine capsules for schools

definitions.meaning: first meaning: single-serve sealed containers of ground coffee
second meaning: groups of whales or dolphins swimming together

explanation.surface: Capsule coffee machines being supplied to schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schools' looks like places of education, but it means groups of sea mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the coffee capsules and the collective term for a herd of whales or dolphins, which also gather in schools.

clue.text: Those wandering around county town for trainer

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap on both sides of the town
wandering letters stray from their places and end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
Ennis is the county town of County Clare in Ireland

explanation.surface: People rambling round a county town, looking for a sports coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' suggests a coach, but here it is the shoe. ENNIS is the county town of County Clare, in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is the British word for a sports shoe or sneaker, the same thing as a tennis shoe.

clue.text: Riviera city — home to European relation

indicators.note: a place that is home to something holds it within

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A city on the Riviera is where a European relative lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the adjective, but it is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Gershwin's turned up, covering for Indian

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ira Gershwin, lyricist brother of George; Ira's

explanation.surface: Gershwin arrives to stand in for an Indian performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious Gershwin is George, but it is his lyricist brother Ira who gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the long draped garment worn by many women from India.

clue.text: Tick in tack? Get away with you!

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

parts.note: tack is horse equipment, of which a saddle is the main piece
a ked is a sheep tick, a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A rider finds a tick in the horse's gear and shoos it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' reads as a moment or a mark, but it is the parasite; tack is riding gear for horses, here the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddle is a colloquial command to leave in a hurry, matching the exclamation telling someone to be off.

clue.text: Knotty problem with load, starting from mid-morning

indicators.note: starting from places one piece at the front, ahead of the other
mid means only the centre letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the central, fourth, letter of morning

indicators.note: a problem is a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A tricky difficulty with a delivery that begins halfway through the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knotty problem' looks like one phrase meaning a puzzle; it splits into the definition and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodal means relating to nodes, and a node is literally a knot, so the adjective fits knotty.

clue.text: Man Ray's art movement keeps Welshmen in check

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to dam a flow is to check or hold it back
Dai is a stock Welsh man's name, so Welshmen are Dais

explanation.surface: An American artist's group keeps some Welsh men under control.
explanation.walkthrough: Dai, the Welsh form of David, is the crossword's standard Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Ray was a leading figure of Dada, the anti-art movement of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Comes into force?

parts.note: surface reading: a law or rule takes effect
setter's reading: a person joins the armed forces

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like legislation taking effect, but 'force' is a military service that a recruit signs up for.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who signs up for the army or navy joins one of the armed forces, literally coming into a force.
